"She's a good friend and had a good win yesterday. She's a dangerous player, so I'm happy with the way I played," Sivasangari told the PSA Squash Tour, after her win over Rachel.
"I'm just happy and looking forward to tomorrow (today)," she added.
3a35952012340522: MANCHESTER: Beset by infighting and off to their worst league start for decades, Manchester United host Bournemouth needing to snap a seven-game winless run to quell talk of another mid-season managerial change.
Michael Carrick's men are 13th in the Premier League and could even drop into the bottom three if results go against them this weekend.
At the other end of the table, Manchester City aim to extend their flawless start to the season at Aston Villa, despite doubts over the club's future in the English top-flight.
Third-placed Brighton are dreaming of an unlikely title challenge but face a stiff examination when they travel to Liverpool.
AFP Sport looks at the pick of the Premier League action this weekend:
Man Utd back in crisis mode
The Red Devils sank to new depths during a terrible start to the season in a 4-1 thrashing by Champions League debutants Como in midweek.
Captain Bruno Fernandes took aim at his manager's passive tactics after the match, saying United had to be more "brave."
But Carrick, who apologised to the travelling fans in Italy, hit back at his players for not covering enough ground.
"Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win," said the former United midfielder.
The blunt remarks come just a week after defender Lisandro Martinez criticised the club's board for not investing enough in the transfer market.
United's return of seven points from their opening seven games is their lowest of the Premier League era.
After the departures of Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim in the past two seasons, United are facing another campaign of transition unless Carrick can quickly right the ship.
Brighton hungry for more
Only Barcelona have outscored Brighton in Europe's top five leagues this season, with the Seagulls netting 23 times in their seven games.
Brighton have soared through the divisions and into Europe on the back of owner Tony Bloom's expertise in data analytics, but they are yet to win a major trophy in their 125-year history.

Matching Leicester's remarkable title triumph a decade ago still seems unlikely, but Brighton will get a clearer idea of where they stand after visits to Anfield and Manchester City in the next two weekends.
Despite routinely selling their prized assets to wealthier clubs, Brighton's smart recruitment of both players and coaches has ensured they have continued to thrive.
"We can enjoy it, but on the other side it's also very important to stay humble and stay grounded because in football things can change quickly," said 33-year-old manager Fabian Hurzeler.
"We have to have this hunger inside of us to keep going and never be satisfied – to keep pushing."
City face Villa Park demons
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca is the first manager to win his first seven Premier League games in charge of a new club.
Yet it may all count for nothing unless City are successful in their appeal after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules.
Maresca's men travel to Aston Villa on Saturday, hoping to improve on a miserable recent record in Birmingham.
City have lost on their past three visits to Villa Park and face a resurgent opponent after an overhaul of Unai Emery's squad in the transfer market.

Villa have won five and drawn one of their past six games in all competitions as new signings Nicolas Jackson, Johan Manzambi and Zion Suzuki have quickly settled in to mitigate the loss of Ollie Watkins, Morgan Rogers and Emi Martinez.
"How we are responding, getting better, is really fantastic," Emery said after Villa beat Viking to make it three wins from three in the Champions League.
"How some individual players are feeling comfortable and getting confidence and getting better rhythm on the field is really as well something (that) makes us happy and confident (in) ourselves."

9c91690e929bf786: BEIJING: At least 16 people were killed and 32 others injured when a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China's remote Tibet region, state news agency Xinhua reported, citing local authorities.
More than 300 houses collapsed in the earthquake, which struck on Thursday at 10.33pm (1433 GMT). Officials were still assessing the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, Xinhua said.
The quake's epicentre was in a mountainous area about 190km east-northeast of Nagqu and 390km northeast of the regional capital, Lhasa, the US Geological Survey said.
It struck at a shallow depth of 10km.
A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said.

The epicentre was located in Maru township in Baqen county. Township deputy head Lhawang Dagpo said the quake was clearly felt at the township office, which sustained cracks in its walls, according to Xinhua.
Power and telecommunications services were disrupted in the county seat, the agency said.
Earthquakes are relatively common in China.
In January 2025, at least 126 people were killed in an earthquake in Tibet's rural Tingri county.

6b442493e249114f: AUSTIN: Isack Hadjar riled rival Charles Leclerc by suggesting Ferrari had the fastest car and Red Bull teammate Max Verstappen would have won this month's Singapore Grand Prix by an even greater margin if he had been driving for the Italian team.
Leclerc, who finished second in the race and 7.3 seconds behind four-time Formula One champion Verstappen, dismissed the Frenchman's claims at the US Grand Prix on Thursday.

"I think it's nonsense to start saying these kinds of things. Isack has no idea what kind of car we drive, and I have no idea what kind of car he drives," the Monegasque told reporters at Austin's Circuit of the Americas.
Hadjar, who finished 10th in Singapore, said the Red Bull car was still very hard to drive even if Verstappen has now won the last two races.

"In Malaysia, it (the Red Bull) was dominant, but I don't think in Singapore it was the fastest car. That's what I believe. I think if you put Max in the Ferrari, he would have won the race with more margin. So that's my opinion. In Singapore, I think it (the Ferrari) was the fastest car," he said.
McLaren's Oscar Piastri said both rivals were stronger than the reigning champions.

"I think it wasn't a surprise that Ferrari were very strong in Singapore. I think on the data analysis, they're always the quickest or joint-quickest or outright quickest in basically every corner this year," the Australian said.

"But they lose on all the straights, whether that's from drag or power, I don't know ... but we've expected them (Ferrari) to be the benchmark at other circuits and it's not turned out to be the case. I think they're very strong. I think clearly Red Bull was very strong. Both stronger than us for sure.
"I think over the last few weeks Red Bull has definitely become the most consistently quick car. But I think each weekend the challenges are kind of rotating."
80f9ed1983cb18fc: NEW YORK: New York's City Council on Thursday voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, signalling the end of a tourist ritual that has been the subject of heated debate for years.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who must sign the measure into law, had previously voiced support for such a ban but has also expressed concerns about protections for workers in the industry.
If the mayor signs it, the ban will take effect in June 2028.
The lead-up period is intended to help the approximately 150 active carriage drivers find new employment, City Council Speaker Julie Menin told journalists ahead of the vote.
The Transport Workers Union, which represents the workers, has vowed to take legal action.
Legislative battles over the fate of the cultural tradition, which is nearly as old as Central Park itself, have been ongoing for nearly two decades.
Critics say the animals suffer, pointing to deadly collapses and dangerous escapes, while advocates highlight the jobs they create and the heritage they uphold.
The bill includes a provision to explore potential compensation for licence holders, Menin said.
It mandates that owners of the nearly 200 horses would not be allowed to sell them for slaughter or to other horse-carriage businesses.

The rides — featured in film and television, including a scene with Robert Redford and Jane Fonda in "Barefoot in the Park" and a dramatic ride in "Sex and the City" — currently cost US$150 for 45 minutes, rising to several hundred dollars for a marriage proposal.
But after years of wrangling over the issue, the summer season proved decisive in sounding the death knell for the Manhattan carriages.
In June, an 18-year-old tourist from India was killed by a horse that broke loose and bolted.
That followed a series of other incidents involving the carriages, including the deaths of several horses.

The Central Park Conservancy, which manages the US's most frequented urban park, with 42 million annual visits, also threw its weight behind calls for a ban, saying it had become "a matter of public health and safety".

f00100f1cd0cfac1: TAIPEI: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, though the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191kph (119 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).
"The storm was about 330km east of Taiwan's southern tip," the CWA said.
The storm's forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.
The administration said its radius was around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.
Taiwan's financial markets will also close on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which sit next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal.
The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights were cancelled for Friday, along with more than 350 international ones.
In the capital Taipei there were squally showers, but public transport including the subway was operating as usual, albeit with reduced service.
Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.
The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.
c93ff11ca6adb1c6: PERFORMING with the Malaysian Philharmonic Orchestra (MPO) was more than just another career milestone for Jaclyn Victor.
It fulfilled a dream she had nurtured since the early days of her career, bringing her signature hits and musical influences together in a celebration of more than two decades of artistic growth.
Held at Dewan Filharmonik Petronas on Oct 17, 'Jaclyn Victor: Gemilang Bersama MPO' featured the singer performing alongside the orchestra under conductor Ahmad Muriz Che Rose.
About 900 people attended the concert, which celebrated Jaclyn's rise to fame and her willingness to challenge herself as a performer
"When I first entered the industry, just hearing the name MPO made me feel intimidated and nervous. It was like walking into a luxury-brand store," she said before the concert.
"Having my own solo concert with the MPO has always been one of my biggest dreams. The MPO is in a league of its own, and I am grateful that this opportunity has finally come."
The night held particular significance for Jaclyn, whose career took off after she won the inaugural season of 'Malaysian Idol' in 2004.
Her powerful rendition of 'Gemilang', composed by Aubrey Suwito with lyrics by Asmin Mudin, became synonymous with her rise to fame and remains one of her signature songs.
More than 20 years later, the song lent its name to her first solo concert with the MPO, giving the familiar anthem a new orchestral setting.
The evening opened with 'This Is Me', the song performed by Keala Settle in 'The Greatest Showman'.
Jaclyn then took the audience back to her Malaysian Idol days with 'Tunggu Sekejap', the Tan Sri P. Ramlee classic she performed during the competition.
"I still remember being challenged to perform this song during P. Ramlee week. It was a memorable moment in my early musical journey."
FAMILIAR SONGS, FRESH PERSPECTIVES
Rather than simply repeating familiar arrangements, the concert allowed Jaclyn to explore how her hits could be transformed by a full orchestra.
Her setlist featured classic tracks such as 'Ikut Rentakku', 'Di Bawah Pohon Asmara', 'Tiada Lagi Indah'and 'Beribu Sesalan', alongside international hits from different eras and genres.
One of her personal highlights was 'Superwoman', the Karyn White hit Jaclyn remembered singing as a teenager.
"I was 15 when this song became popular. It was one of my favourite songs, and I used to sing it all the time."
The show also paid tribute to iconic voices that shaped her style, including Aretha Franklin, Whitney Houston, Mariah Carey, Celine Dion and Beyonce.
Showstoppers like 'Natural Woman', 'Hero', 'When You Believe', 'I Surrender' and 'Listen' allowed Jaclyn to revisit celebrated diva repertoire and showcase her vocal range.
Her performance of 'Cheek to Cheek', the jazz standard written by Irving Berlin and made famous by Fred Astaire, added a stylish change of pace.
Yet, it was perhaps the trickier numbers that best showed what this collaboration was all about.
"Abang Muriz likes to challenge me to try something new. I am not a classical singer, but I welcome the opportunity to push the boundaries of my vocal abilities," Jaclyn said before the concert.
STEPPING OUTSIDE HER COMFORT ZONE
One of the night's most anticipated challenges was 'O Mio Babbino Caro', the famous opera aria by Giacomo Puccini.
Jaclyn also took on 'Time to Say Goodbye', a track made famous by classical crossover legends.
Before the concert, she acknowledged that performing with a full orchestra could be daunting and required intense focus and control.
"Every emotional nuance and breath matters when performing with a full orchestra. The audience can hear the smallest details, so I need to remain focused and in control throughout," she said.
Jaclyn rose to the occasion withΒ 'O Mio Babbino Caro', while her solo rendition of 'Beribu Sesalan' demonstrated her ability to carry a song associated with multiple singers.
She even surprised the crowd with 'Chong Bai', the popular Mandarin hit by Taiwanese singer Fish Leong.
For Muriz, the aim was not simply to pair a celebrated singer with a full orchestra, but to explore what she could achieve beyond her familiar repertoire.
"Everyone knows the strength and power of Jaclyn's voice. For this concert at DFP, I wanted to challenge her to step outside her comfort zone and try something unexpected," he said before the show.
The concert also featured new symphonic arrangements by Aubrey Suwito, Luqman Aziz, Gerard Salonga, Shahhakam Mokhtar, Teuku Umar Ilany, Leonard Yeap and Muriz himself.
The arrangements added fresh layers to Jaclyn's repertoire.
A JOURNEY THAT CONTINUES
Despite the musical risks, the evening remained anchored by the anthem that launched Jaclyn's career.
Jaclyn closed her main set with 'Gemilang', bringing the evening full circle to the song that first put her on the map.
She returned for two encore performances, 'When I Fall in Love' and 'Di Bawah Pohon Asmara'.
Jaclyn also took a moment to chat with the audience, joking that she was delighted so many people had turned up despite the haze affecting the country.
The light-hearted remark offered a glimpse of Jaclyn's charm, complementing a performance that demanded considerable technical skill.
Jaclyn's concert places her among Malaysian singers who have performed with the MPO, including the late Tan Sri S.M. Salim, Datuk Seri Sheila Majid, Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza and Datuk M. Nasir.
But 'Gemilang Bersama MPO' was, above all, a persona triumph, allowing her to honour her past while pushing her limits in the present.
The title 'Gemilang', meaning 'glorious', has long been associated with Jaclyn's musical journey.
On the DFP stage, the song served as a reminder that success does not mean standing still.

More than two decades after her win, Jaclyn remains eager to learn, experiment and take risks, showing that even an established singer can discover new possibilities by stepping beyond her comfort zone.

9c3929e6f427360e: PETALING JAYA: Young voters in Melaka want better-paying jobs and affordable homes, but whether these concerns will determine how they vote on Nov 14 remains to be seen.
Masjid Tanah MP Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said the issue was not simply about creating employment, but also about ensuring young adults earn enough to raise families and build a future in the state.
The Wanita Wawasan chief said many in this voter segment were looking beyond political parties and personalities for leaders who understood the challenges they faced.
“What they are asking for is a government that understands their struggles and also takes their future seriously,” she told FMT.
Mas Ermieyati urged young voters to question candidates and demand accountability, warning political parties not to treat them as mere election statistics.
Melaka has 687,697 registered voters for the state election, an increase of 192,502, or 38.9%, from 495,195 in 2021.
Electoral reform group Tindak Malaysia estimates that 35.3% of the additional voters are aged below 30.

However, International Islamic University Malaysia political analyst Syaza Shukri believes pro-Malay sentiment among Malay voters, and anti-government sentiment among the non-Malays, may carry more weight than economic concerns.
She said many young voters relied heavily on social media for political information but were not equipped to properly evaluate the policies put forward by the competing parties.
“Young voters still lack political awareness, and whether we like it or not, political sentiment will have a bigger influence on their votes, as seen in Johor and Negeri Sembilan,” she told FMT.
Syaza said such sentiment could influence both Malay and non-Malay voters, pointing to support for Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional in the two most recent state elections.
Despite this, Syaza acknowledged that a sizeable segment of the electorate was also looking for political stability, although their expectations have changed since the 2021 Melaka election.

At the time, many voters were looking for an administration that could manage the economic fallout from the Covid-19 pandemic while avoiding unnecessary political upheaval and leadership changes, she said.
Today, she said, their focus is on economic growth and improving purchasing power.
Syaza said the message that a stable government could deliver economic progress had resonated with voters in Johor, and suggested it could also influence voters in Melaka.
Young voters could decide close contests
Meanwhile, Universiti Sains Malaysia's Sivamurugan Pandian said young voters could be key to determining the outcome in seats won by narrow margins in 2021.
He said young people were increasingly willing to judge parties on their ability to deliver, rather than remain loyal to a particular coalition or party.
Sivamurugan said that BN would rely on its grassroots machinery to woo young voters, while Pakatan Harapan will refer to its reform agenda and an emphasis on inclusive governance.
PAS, on the other hand, will hope to attract those looking for an alternative.
However, he said it was still unclear how many registered voters lived outside Melaka and whether they would return to vote.
In 2021, BN won Serkam by just 79 votes, Pengkalan Batu by 131, and Duyong (200).

Namun, penganalisis politik dari Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia, Syaza Shukri, percaya sentimen pro-Melayu dalam kalangan pengundi Melayu serta sentimen antikerajaan dalam kalangan pengundi bukan Melayu mungkin membawa pengaruh lebih besar, berbanding kebimbangan ekonomi.
Beliau berkata, ramai pengundi muda bergantung pada media sosial untuk mendapatkan maklumat politik, namun tidak mempunyai keupayaan menilai dasar dikemukakan parti bertanding.

“Pengundi muda masih kurang kesedaran politik dan suka atau tidak, sentimen politik akan memberi pengaruh lebih besar terhadap undi mereka, seperti dapat dilihat di Johor dan Negeri Sembilan,” katanya kepada FMT.
Syaza berkata, sentimen sedemikian mampu mempengaruhi pengundi Melayu mahupun bukan Melayu, sambil merujuk sokongan terhadap Barisan Nasional (BN) dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) pada dua PRN lalu.
Bagaimanapun, Syaza mengakui sebilangan besar pengundi juga mahukan kestabilan politik, walaupun jangkaan mereka telah berubah berbanding PRN Melaka pada 2021.

Ketika itu, ramai pengundi mencari pentadbiran yang mampu menguruskan kesan ekonomi akibat pandemik Covid-19, selain mengelakkan pergolakan politik dan pertukaran kepimpinan yang tidak perlu, katanya.
Hari ini, katanya, fokus mereka tertumpu kepada pertumbuhan ekonomi dan peningkatan kuasa beli.
Syaza berkata, mesej kestabilan kerajaan mampu membawa kemajuan ekonomi diterima baik pengundi Johor, dan percaya ia juga akan mempengaruhi pengundi di Melaka.
Pengundi muda penentu saingan sengit
Sementara itu, Sivamurugan Pandian dari Universiti Sains Malaysia, berkata pengundi muda dilihat akan menjadi penentu keputusan di kerusi dimenangi majoriti tipis, pada 2021.
Beliau berkata, golongan muda kini semakin bersedia menilai parti berdasarkan keupayaan mereka menunaikan janji, berbanding kekal setia kepada sesebuah gabungan atau parti tertentu.

Sivamurugan berkata, BN akan bergantung pada jentera akar umbinya untuk memikat pengundi muda, manakala Pakatan Harapan (PH) pula dijangka mengemukakan agenda reformasi serta penekanan terhadap tadbir urus inklusif.
PAS sebaliknya berharap dapat menarik minat mereka yang mencari alternatif lain.
Katanya, masih belum jelas berapa ramai pengundi berdaftar yang menetap di luar Melaka dan sama ada mereka akan pulang memilih.
Pada 2021, BN menang kerusi Serkam dengan hanya 79 undi, Pengkalan Batu dengan 131 undi, dan Duyong, 200 undi.
2f3905d621608ec9: PETALING JAYA: Is James Gunn’s DC Universe already losing momentum? Following the success of “Superman” last year, fans were eager to see what the new DCU had in store, particularly with a slate of projects promising characters and stories rarely explored on the big screen.

Then came Craig Gillespie’s “Supergirl”, starring Milly Alcock, which failed to make a strong impression at the box office earlier this year and divided cinemagoers. Now, James Watkins’s “Clayface”, billed as the DCU’s first proper foray into horror, risks following a similarly uncertain path.

The 109-minute film, starring Welsh actor Tom Rhys Harries in the title role, feels less like a major DC release and more like a B-grade companion piece. That is not necessarily a problem - in fact, a smaller, stranger genre film could have been exactly what the character needed.

But for a body-horror story centred on one of DC Comics’ best-known villains - and based on a script originally written by acclaimed horror filmmaker Mike Flanagan - “Clayface” feels surprisingly cautious. It rarely pushes the grotesque possibilities of its premise far enough, and it also remains oddly detached from the wider world of DC superheroes.

The story follows Matt Hagen (Harries), an aspiring actor whose promising career is shattered after a brutal attack leaves his face disfigured. Desperate to reclaim both his appearance and livelihood, he turns to an experimental procedure developed by Dr Caitlin Bates (Naomi Ackie), which promises to restore what he has lost.
Instead, the treatment transforms him into a shape-shifting creature capable of moulding his body into different forms.
At its core, “Clayface” follows a familiar villain-origin arc, asking how far someone might fall when stripped of identity, purpose and hope.

Harries sells that descent convincingly. There is a degree of catharsis when Hagen finally exacts revenge, and the filmmakers clearly want his transformation to feel psychologically rooted rather than merely monstrous.

The problem is that the film keeps reaching for complexity without ever fully committing to it. Bates, in particular, feels underwritten, despite being central to Hagen’s transformation. Her motivations and personal stakes are never explored deeply enough, leaving what should be a fraught relationship feeling thinner than it ought to.

The script also gestures towards weightier ideas about scientific ethics, ambition, vanity and the lengths people will go to recover what they have lost. Yet these themes are introduced more often than they are developed, which makes several of the characters’ choices feel less compelling than intended.
The pacing does not help: “Clayface” frequently meanders, with too little danger or urgency to sustain tension.

There are moments of gore, certainly, but the body horror rarely reaches the disturbing heights the concept invites. For a story built around grotesque transformation and the loss of bodily control, the film should feel far more unsettling than it does.
One of the brighter spots is its portrayal of Gotham. Batman is never mentioned, but the city itself is recognisable: grimy, dangerous and crawling with criminals.

Its brooding atmosphere gives “Clayface” a sense of place that much of the rest of the film lacks. This, however, only makes it more frustrating that the story never quite establishes how Hagen fits into this world, or whether he is meant to matter beyond this standalone outing.

For now, the film feels suspended between two identities: a grim body-horror experiment and a comic-book origin story. It never fully commits to either - and that indecision ultimately becomes its defining flaw.
"Clayface" wants to disturb, move and intrigue, but instead leaves its horror ambitions, and its place in the DC universe, frustratingly unresolved.
As of press time, ‘Clayface’ is screening in cinemas nationwide.

9c96626421bd32c1: SAN ISIDRO: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on Dec 22, the court announced Thursday, after six months of hearings.
The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star's death concluded Thursday with brief statements from Maradona's daughter and some of the defendants.
"I hope my father receives the justice he deserves...like anyone else," said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion.
The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona's primary doctor, declared: "I am innocent."
Maradona died at age 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary edema.
He was found dead in his bed on November 25, 2020, at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence, following minor neurosurgery.
His death plunged the country into mourning in the midst of the Covid-19 pandemic.
Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to twelve years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence - 12 years - sought for Luque.
In closing arguments Wednesday, Luque's defence attorneys rejected the prosecution's argument that Maradona's death was foreseeable, calling their client a "scapegoat" in the case.
7277351cf346e5c7: CARACAS: Thousands of Venezuelans took to the streets on Thursday in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years, as demonstrators demanded free elections and other political changes with a notably thin presence of security forces.
The US has been working closely with the interim government led by acting president Delcy Rodriguez since US forces captured president Nicolas Maduro in January.
Both US president Donald Trump and Rodriguez, Maduro's former deputy, have said there will be elections, but have not set a date either for a legislative vote or a national contest for president.

Opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado, who has been outside the country for nearly a year after living in hiding following a contested 2024 election, has said elections must take place by July 2027.
Her Vente Venezuela movement organised the protest, which took place in the capital Caracas and other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo.
“Seeing this makes me happy because I know change is possible," said 18-year-old cosmetology student Leosmary Hernandez, as she gathered with hundreds of others in northern Maracay.
"I’ve been through so many hardships, so many problems because of the dollar, and difficulties studying. I have high hopes for my country and for our next leader, president, Maria Corina," she said.
"I went out to protest before, when things were much tougher, and I’m even less afraid today because I want my voice to be heard,” she added as music boomed around protesters waving Venezuelan flags.

Venezuela's socialist movement, in power since 1999 under late president Hugo Chavez and then Maduro, has in the past deployed security forces against protesters decrying political repression, dizzying inflation, poor public services and other problems in the economically battered country, including after the 2024 presidential election.
Security forces had minimal presence at protest sites on Thursday, and in many smaller cities demonstrators dispersed before dark.

The ruling Socialist Party called for its supporters to march from Caracas' Plaza Venezuela, the same place the opposition planned to gather two hours later, to a location near the presidential palace to commemorate Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

Interior minister Diosdado Cabello, known for his close ties to the security services, was pictured on state television attending the march, while the opposition supporters moved their protest to a nearby location.
Negotiations continue

US-backed talks between a faction of the opposition and the interim government, aimed at remaking the top court and the electoral council with an eye toward ensuring fairness at eventual elections, held their latest session this month, but changes could take significant time.
The negotiations do not include Machado's political movement, though she has said she will not stand in the way of their progress.
Machado's proxy roundly won the 2024 election according to vote tallies released by the opposition.
However, the government, which never released full counts, backed Maduro, as did the country's legal and electoral institutions.

"We want presidential elections now. We want an electoral timetable to be announced now. We are not going to wait until 2028," said Maria Debora Marin, 57, who runs a clothing store in central Valencia, referring to rumors that elections may only take place the year after next. "What we want is to move forward and finally get out of this nightmare," she said.
Amid the arrests of some of her closest collaborators, Machado went into hiding.
Her last public appearance in Venezuela was at protests to mark Maduro's third inauguration in January 2025, where she was briefly detained.
Machado has for years sought US support, aligning with hawks in the Trump team who argued that Maduro — through links to drug gangs — represented a direct threat to US national security.
Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, are facing drug and torture charges in the US. They have pleaded not guilty.
However, Trump has repeatedly praised Rodriguez's management and her willingness to welcome US investors, saying last month it is too soon to consider elections.
Machado's desire to return home, especially after devastating twin earthquakes in June, has caused friction in Washington, with US officials asking her to delay her trip, Reuters has reported.
"We're in limbo," said recent graduate Rayeska Puesme, 18, as she attended the protest in Caracas, adding she had considered leaving because of a lack of opportunities.
"The US removed one big problem, which was Maduro, but the rest are still there," she said.
"I feel in my heart that things are going to change, but I don't see when," she added.
Demonstrators were also calling for the release of prisoners they say are held for political reasons.

Legal rights group Foro Penal, which represents opposition figures and others who have been detained, often on charges like treason, says there are still more than 320 political prisoners in Venezuela, despite releases that took place under an amnesty law backed by the legislature earlier this year.
The government has repeatedly denied holding political prisoners and says the amnesty is generous.
18461239a4440a16: SAN ISIDRO: The verdict in the trial over the 2020 death of Argentine football legend Diego Maradona will be delivered on Dec 22, the court announced on Thursday, after six months of hearings.
The trial of seven healthcare professionals accused of negligence in the star's death concluded on Thursday with brief statements from Maradona's daughter and some of the defendants.
"I hope my father receives the justice he deserves... like anyone else," said Dalma Maradona, her voice breaking with emotion.
The main defendant in the case, Leopoldo Luque, Maradona's primary doctor, declared: "I am innocent."
Maradona died at the age of 60 from heart failure coupled with pulmonary oedema.
He was found dead in his bed on Nov 25, 2020, at a residence in Tigre, north of Buenos Aires, rented for his convalescence following minor neurosurgery.
His death plunged the country into mourning amid the Covid-19 pandemic.
Prosecutors requested prison sentences ranging from four to 12 years for six of the seven defendants, with the heaviest sentence — 12 years — sought for Luque.
In closing arguments on Wednesday, Luque's defence attorneys rejected the prosecution's argument that Maradona's death was foreseeable, calling their client a "scapegoat" in the case.
80a2e00af8b1eb86: KUALA LUMPUR: Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah are chasing successive World Tour titles for the first time, but the effects of a demanding tournament schedule are beginning to take their toll.
The world No. 4 kept their hopes alive after overcoming younger compatriots Ong Xin Yee-Carmen Ting 21-14, 22-20 in 46 minutes to reach the French Open quarter-finals on Thursday.
Pearly-Thinaah, the Denmark Open winners last week, were made to work harder in the second game before sealing victory at Arena Grand Paris.
However, Pearly admitted that they were far from their physical best after a busy schedule that included the China Masters and Asian Games last month, followed by back-to-back tournaments in Europe.

"I don't think physically we are very good. It's very obvious in the match, but we just keep reminding each other, believing in each other and trying to support each other," said Pearly in a post-match interview with the Badminton World Federation.
Although Pearly-Thinaah won three World Tour titles last year, at the Thailand Open, Arctic Open and Kumamoto Masters, they have never won titles at consecutive tournaments.
Their Denmark Open success, which ended an eight-month wait for another title, has given them an opportunity to achieve that milestone.
Standing in their way in Friday's quarter-finals are Bulgaria's eighth seeds Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva.

The Malaysians hold a 4-1 head-to-head advantage over the world No. 9 Bulgarian sisters, having won their most recent encounter 21-15, 21-10 in the quarter-finals of last year's World Championships, also held in Paris.
Thinaah expects another physically demanding encounter, particularly with the slower shuttle conditions at the venue.
"We have to be really patient because they are physically very good and powerful," said Thinaah.
"With the slow conditions, we just have to prepare ourselves physically and mentally."
Pearly-Thinaah, who captured their breakthrough Super 750 title at the French Open in 2022, have yet to drop a game in Paris this week.

eff83b2d2cde32aa: KUALA LUMPUR: Young gibbons are being hidden in suitcases and smuggled on passenger flights, with Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) the most frequently implicated airport in a new study.
The wildlife trade monitoring organisation Traffic recorded at least 86 gibbons intercepted in 33 airport smuggling incidents linked to Southeast Asia between January 2024 and last August.
KLIA was linked to 16 cases involving at least 54 gibbons, including 32 seized at the airport.
The animals were concealed in pet carriers or plastic baskets inside checked-in luggage. Every gibbon whose life stage was known was an infant or juvenile, read the report.
Demand for exotic pets helps drive the trade, although investigators must establish whether particular shipments were intended for pet owners or captive facilities.
Traffic Southeast Asia director Kanitha Krishnasamy warned that small shipments could cause devastating losses.
"The smuggling of just a few gibbons on each flight may seem small in isolation, but like a dripping tap, the losses accumulate over time.
"What appears minor can add up to a devastating toll on wild populations," she said.
The report also documented seven gibbons found dead in May last year after reportedly being flown from Malaysia in suitcases.
Adults may be harmed or killed when young gibbons are captured, adding to losses beyond the animals seized.
At least 38 people were arrested in connection with the airport incidents. Some couriers were allegedly offered cash, flights and accommodation to transport wildlife.
Traffic warned that detected cases likely underestimated the trade's true scale and called for stronger airport screening and investigations targeting trafficking networks.
c4970f5b53d6d7da: WASHINGTON: The US government will increase measures aimed at preventing entry by people exposed to Ebola with a new requirement for US-bound air travellers to attest they have not been in the Democratic Republic of Congo in the prior 21 days, according to a memo on Thursday seen by Reuters.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in May adopted rules barring ‌airline passengers who have been in the DRC, the centre of the 2026 outbreak, in the prior three weeks. The restrictions were extended to US citizens in July.
The new CDC order takes effect Nov 3 and requires all US-bound airline passengers to file digital or paper attestations.
Airlines for America, which represents United Airlines, American Airlines, Southwest Airlines and Delta Air Lines, did not immediately comment.
The CDC is holding briefing calls with major US and foreign airlines on Friday to detail how carriers should comply with the new requirements.
As part of the Ebola measures, the CDC since earlier this year has also barred foreign nationals from the US if they have been in Uganda or South Sudan in the prior three weeks.
The Bundibugyo strain of the virus spread undetected for months before ​the outbreak was declared in May. It kills about half of those infected and has no approved treatment or vaccine.
So far the outbreak is confirmed to have killed about 4,700 people in Africa, according to the Africa CDC.
To date, no Ebola cases associated with this outbreak have been reported in the United States, the CDC said.
c7a60da5da114a53: PETALING JAYA: Bersatu akan sukar mengulangi pencapaian Perikatan Nasional (PN) pada pilihan raya lalu tanpa PAS, sekalipun dengan gagasan dan hala tuju baharu serta komposisi majmuk, menurut penganalisis.
Tawfik Yaakub daripada Universiti Malaya berkata selama ini 'Perikatan Nasional' adalah jenama yang disokong kekuatan akar umbi dan jentera PAS, serta pengaruh pemimpin parti itu.
"Jenama PN mungkin boleh dihidupkan semula, tetapi kekuatan politik yang dibina bersama PAS tidak semestinya dapat diwarisi secara automatik," katanya kepada FMT.

Tawfik mengulas kenyataan pengasas bersama Bersatu, Redzuan Yusof, yang tidak menolak kemungkinan Bersatu mengambil inisiatif untuk membentuk semula 'Perikatan Nasional' menerusi Ikatan Prihatin Rakyat (IPR), yang menurutnya berpotensi dijenamakan semula sebagai PN.
Dipengerusikan Presiden Bersatu Muhyiddin Yassin, IPR merupakan gabungan longgar parti-parti pembangkang.

Ketika pelancarannya, IPR menghimpunkan pemimpin daripada PN serta parti-parti kecil seperti Parti Bumiputera Perkasa Malaysia (Putra), Barisan Jemaah Islamiah Se-Malaysia (Berjasa) dan Parti Perikatan India Muslim Nasional (Iman); Parti Kemajuan Malaysia (MAP) dan Parti Bersepakat Hak Rakyat Malaysia (Urimai); dan Ikatan Demokratik Malaysia (Muda).

Kemungkinan yang disuarakan Redzuan itu menyusuli tindakan Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan Malaysia (JPPM) membatalkan pendaftaran PN, ekoran aduan Bersatu yang menurut Setiausaha Agungnya Mohamed Azmin Ali berkenaan pelanggaran perlembagaan PN oleh kepimpinan baharu PN.
Perkembangan ini berlatarkan perselisihan antara Bersatu dan PAS.
Bagaimanapun, Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur semalam membenarkan permohonan PN untuk menggantung pelaksanaan keputusan JPPM itu.
Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia menjangkakan perebutan yang sengit antara Bersatu dan PAS untuk jenama PN.
"Kalau betul ini berlaku akan menjadi masalah dan perebutan dengan PAS kerana PAS pula mengharapkan nama PN itu dapat menarik sokongan bukan Melayu," katanya kepada FMT.
Syaza percaya Bersatu cenderung kepada jenama PN memandangkan pembina jenama IPR dalam kalangan pengundi akan memerlukan masa, sedangkan ia perlu bersedia menghadapi pilihan raya akan datang.

Tawfik pula melihat IPR sebagai alternatif untuk Bersatu membina platform yang lebih inklusif dan merentasi kaum. "IPR masih belum mempunyai pengaruh politik, kekuatan organisasi dan tahap pengenalan jenama yang sama seperti PN."
"Kewujudan parti yang mewakili pelbagai komuniti juga tidak menjamin sokongan pengundi bukan Melayu secara automatik," katanya.
Sekiranya Bersatu berjaya mengambil jenama PN, ia perlu membuktikan PN masih mempunyai sokongan rakyat, jentera, dan kepimpinan yang mampu menyatukan parti komponen, tanpa PAS.

"Isu utamanya bukan sekadar sama ada Bersatu boleh menggunakan semula jenama PN, tetapi sama ada pengundi masih menerima identiti politik tersebut apabila komposisi gabungannya sudah berubah," kata Tawfik.
fded7086a292b866: PETALING JAYA: You've paid for your holiday accommodation, enjoyed a few restful days and packed your bags - only to discover that checking out involves stripping the beds, doing the laundry and taking out the rubbish.
For travellers who have encountered such demands at short-term rental properties, Airbnb's latest global policy changes could come as welcome news.

The accommodation platform announced on Oct 20 that it would restrict the household chores hosts can require guests to perform, particularly tasks that demand considerable time or would ordinarily be handled by professional cleaners.
The updated rules will apply to reservations booked on or after Nov 20, affecting Airbnb hosts and guests internationally, including those using the platform in Malaysia.
Under the new policy, hosts will generally be prohibited from requiring guests to strip beds, start laundry, wash and put away dishes, or dispose of rubbish outside the property.

However, this doesn't mean visitors can abandon all responsibility for keeping their accommodation reasonably tidy. Hosts may still request simpler tasks, such as placing dirty dishes in the sink, gathering used towels, or separating rubbish into designated indoor bins.

Airbnb also distinguishes between restricting an advertised amenity and asking guests to use it responsibly. For example, hosts cannot prohibit guests from using air conditioning that forms part of the listing, but may ask them to switch it off when leaving.
The company said it had received feedback that house rules could be confusing, burdensome and difficult to manage, prompting an overhaul intended to make expectations clearer.
No more unpleasant surprises

Another significant change concerns how rules are communicated to guests, with Airbnb requiring hosts to disclose all house rules and requests in designated sections of their listings before reservations are made.
These conditions can no longer be introduced unexpectedly through private messages, notices inside the property or verbal instructions after booking.
Hosts will be able to choose from seven standard categories covering matters such as overnight guest limits, pets, smoking, quiet hours, events and locking up at checkout.

The platform will further assess additional requests for reasonableness, taking into account the type of accommodation and relevant local circumstances. Exceptions may be permitted, such as special waste-disposal arrangements in areas where wildlife poses a problem.

Hosts whose requests breach the policy may receive warnings or be asked to revise their listings. Persistent violations could result in notices appearing on the property listing or reduced visibility in Airbnb searches.

The changes have already sparked criticism among Airbnb hosts, some of whom argue that restricting basic checkout chores could increase cleaning costs, create hygiene problems and complicate preparations for incoming guests.
Disgruntled hosts have taken to online forums to express their frustration, with some even threatening to abandon the platform.
Travellers, meanwhile, have largely welcomed the move, questioning why they should be expected to perform household chores when cleaning fees are already part of their accommodation costs.
What about Malaysian stays?
For Malaysians booking apartments, holiday homes or other accommodation through Airbnb, the changes offer greater clarity about what is expected before departure.
This could be particularly relevant to families or groups renting entire properties, where cleaning instructions sometimes form part of the checkout arrangements.
Malaysian hosts, meanwhile, may need to review their listings and distinguish reasonable housekeeping requests from duties that should be handled between guest stays.
Ultimately, the principle is straightforward: a holiday rental should come with clear responsibilities, not an unexpected list of domestic chores.
ab004f619c0b5081: The renminbi is back at the centre of debates about global macroeconomic imbalances. With China’s merchandise trade surplus widening to US$1.2 trillion in 2025, and with its manufacturing sector becoming increasingly dominant, the near-consensus among financial and economic commentators is that the renminbi is significantly undervalued.

The implication is that China should let its currency appreciate sharply, thereby shrinking its surplus, easing competitive pressure on manufacturers elsewhere, and helping rebalance the global economy.

This argument is politically convenient, because it points to a seemingly painless solution. Unfortunately, it suffers from a fatal flaw. Before simply assuming that exchange-rate appreciation is appropriate for China, one must examine the underlying cause of the currency’s weakness.

If it was primarily the result of deliberate interventions to expand exports, rapid appreciation would indeed be a relatively clean remedy. But if it reflects weak domestic demand, allowing the currency to appreciate without addressing the underlying weakness would be counterproductive.
China falls into the second category. The renminbi’s weakness and the widening surplus are better understood as parallel consequences of a deep adjustment in the real-estate sector.

Property was once a central engine of Chinese demand, credit creation, local-government finance, household wealth, and investment. When the property market suffers, so does domestic demand, particularly investment demand. And when investment falls faster than national saving, the external surplus rises.

China is not unusual in this respect. CF40 Research has identified a clear pattern: housing busts have improved economies’ external balances. That is what happened previously in the US and Japan, where weak domestic demand also led to persistently low inflation.

While the renminbi’s nominal exchange rate has been quite stable against both the US dollar and a basket of currencies in recent years, high global inflation and low domestic inflation have produced a large real depreciation. It is not a weak currency that has undermined domestic demand and led to large external surpluses; it is the opposite.

The renminbi’s exchange rate matters, but how it adjusts matters more. An appreciation driven by an economic recovery would be welcome. If the property sector stabilises, household confidence improves, productive investment rises, and imports grow, the currency would strengthen as part of the broader rebalancing.

But too abrupt an appreciation would not repair China’s property market or revive domestic demand. On the contrary, it would hurt the export sector and the investment and consumption that it supports.
The impact on global imbalances would be ambiguous, but it would almost certainly slow China’s recovery, potentially leading to weaker growth for a world economy that would be no less unbalanced.

The rest of the world therefore has a big stake in how China adjusts. China has become a price anchor for a large part of global manufacturing, since producer prices increasingly shape goods prices elsewhere, even when the final product is not imported directly from China.

In fact, weak Chinese demand and a low renminbi exchange rate have helped restrain goods inflation in advanced economies, though this benefit receives far less attention than the competitive pressure China places on foreign producers.

The post-Covid disinflation in advanced economies was a case in point. It came not only from tighter monetary policies and repaired supply chains, but also from soft Chinese manufactured-goods prices.
Sharp currency appreciation would push in the opposite direction, raising the price of Chinese exports. The result would feel less like a painless rebalancing than a cost-push shock.

Such an adjustment would not promote factory construction in Europe, higher productivity in the US, or improvements in China’s property market. It would simply increase the global prices of manufactured goods at a time when inflation in many advanced economies remains elevated. Some foreign producers might welcome the easing of Chinese competition, but central banks’ job would get harder.

Bond markets would also feel the effects. Expectations of higher inflation and tighter monetary policy would increase pressure on nominal yields at a time when advanced economies are already drawing down global savings.

With the US running large fiscal deficits, Europe preparing for more spending on defense and infrastructure, and AI investments creating enormous demand for capital, the need for savings from the rest of the world has grown.

In this context, one must remember that China’s surplus is the counterpart of Chinese net savings supplied to the rest of the world. If China absorbs more at home, less Chinese savings will be available to finance deficits abroad.
That could drive a healthy adjustment if deficit countries were to save more and borrow less. But failing that, bond yields—which have already climbed to multi-year highs—must continue to rise.
None of this means that China should hold down its currency artificially. Rather, it should try to rebalance by strengthening domestic demand.
That means stabilising the property sector, improving household income expectations, expanding social insurance, and shifting investment towards more productive uses.
Such policies would narrow the surplus more durably than exchange-rate adjustment alone. The renminbi would duly strengthen as the recovery takes hold.

But deficit countries have responsibilities, too. They cannot demand smaller Chinese surpluses while continuing to count on cheap imported goods, disinflationary pressure, and abundant foreign savings. If advanced economies want China to absorb more of what it produces, they must show more fiscal discipline themselves.
Kai Guo is executive president and senior fellow of the CF40 Institute.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
f92fbd2a7366c015: TAIPEI: Almost all of Taiwan shut down on Friday ahead of the arrival of Typhoon Champi, which is forecast to bring strong winds and torrential rain, although the storm is weakening and is not expected to make direct landfall on the island.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191kph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).

The storm was about 330km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. Its forecast track shows it will pass just off northeastern Taiwan, turn north towards the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.
The administration said its radius was around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.
Taiwan's financial markets will also close on Friday, while only the Taiwan-controlled Kinmen islands, which lie next to the Chinese coast, will open schools and offices as normal.
The transport ministry said all 262 domestic flights scheduled for Friday had been cancelled, along with more than 350 international flights.
Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, helping to keep casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn, bringing strong winds and torrential rain.
The typhoon is forecast to first pass over Japan's westernmost inhabited island, Yonaguni, in Okinawa Prefecture.
fb6e62db47e2be37: WASHINGTON: Versatile actor Tom Skerritt, who starred in Hollywood megahits including the sci-fi classic "Alien", the war comedy "M*A*S*H" and the action drama "Top Gun", has died at the age of 93.
Skerritt, a Detroit native whose Hollywood career spanned from the 1960s to the 2020s, died on Wednesday of natural causes, his family said in a statement.

"While the world knew Tom through his remarkable acting career, we knew him for his humor, curiosity, wisdom, generosity, and the love he brought into our lives," they said. "He cared deeply about imagination, creativity, storytelling, service, veterans, the natural world, and helping others find and share their own voices."
Known for his rugged good looks and ability to shine in a variety of genres, Skerritt delivered memorable performances in leading and supporting roles in film and television.

Skerritt's breakthrough role was that of a roguish US Army surgeon in director Robert Altman's 1970 Korean War black comedy "M*A*S*H", a film whose ensemble cast also included Donald Sutherland, Elliott Gould and Sally Kellerman. Skerritt played Southerner Duke Forrest as the doctors at the Mobile Army Surgical Hospital stitched up wounded troops.
The film, whose popularity coincided with American unease over the Vietnam War, was nominated for five Academy Awards.

In director Ridley Scott's claustrophobic 1979 sci-fi horror film "Alien", Skerritt played Dallas, the captain of an ill-fated spacecraft whose crew encounters a deadly parasitic extraterrestrial creature with a surrealist look and a bad attitude. In the film's famous and bloody "chestburster" scene, Skerritt's character is seated next to castmate John Hurt when a baby alien violently exits Hurt's character's torso.
"Alien", an influential masterpiece whose ensemble cast also included Sigourney Weaver and Ian Holm, earned two Oscar nominations.

"It is spontaneity and impulse that make the difference, and that is what I felt we had with 'Alien'. Every one of us had that immediate rapport with each other — the respect that I had for the other actors and the respect that they had for me," Skerritt told interviewer Peter Sobczynski in 2019, while also lauding Scott's directorial brilliance.
"Alien" was one of several films in which Skerritt appeared that featured strong female characters, in this case Weaver's courageous character, Ripley. That was considered pioneering at the time.
"When I read the script, one of the things that I liked most about it was that the woman becomes the hero. I loved that," Skerritt said.

"The sight of women being in positions of strength and fortitude to make the right connections and decisions was what appealed to me. I experienced that as well in 'Steel Magnolias', with the women in that. I liked the idea of women being tough and strong and influential."
In "Steel Magnolias" (1989), Skerritt played Drum Eatenton, husband of Sally Field's M'Lynn Eatenton.

Tony Scott, the brother of the "Alien" director, cast Skerritt in the key supporting role of naval aviation instructor Viper Metcalf in the 1986 blockbuster "Top Gun", which helped star Tom Cruise soar into Hollywood's stratosphere.

Skerritt also played Shirley MacLaine's husband in director Herbert Ross's 1977 ballet drama "The Turning Point" and starred alongside another emerging star, Brad Pitt, in Robert Redford's beautifully shot 1992 period drama "A River Runs Through It".

Among the other films in which he appeared were "Harold and Maude" (1971), "Ice Castles" (1978), "The Dead Zone" (1983), "Poltergeist III" (1988), "Contact" (1997), "Tears of the Sun" (2003) and "Ted" (2012).

On the small screen, Skerritt starred in the offbeat CBS series "Picket Fences" from 1992 to 1996, playing a Wisconsin town sheriff and winning an Emmy for outstanding lead actor in a drama series in 1993.

Born on August 25, 1933, in Detroit, Skerritt served in the US Air Force before becoming an actor, making his film debut in 1962 alongside a young Redford in "War Hunt". He was a father of five children and was married three times.
8843a8d923672540: PETALING JAYA: Malaysian doubles shuttlers across all categories continued to shine at the French Open with five pairs storming into the quarter-finals of the World Tour Super 750 championships.
Men’s doubles pair Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun defeated 13th-ranked Japanese pair Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi in straight games 25-23, 21-14 in 41 minutes at the Arena Grand Paris early this morning.

The world No 11 duo, who were first-round casualties at the Denmark Open last week, will clash with world No 4 compatriots Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik, who advanced to the quarter-finals after a walkover from their Thai opponents, Peeratchai Sukphun-Pakkapon Teeraratsakul.
This assures Malaysia of a semi-final spot at the prestigious championships.
World No 5 Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani took 50 minutes to overcome 12th ranked Danish pair Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard 21-6, 14-21, 21-18 in their second-round clash.
Sze Fei-Izzuddin have now won four of their eight encounters so far.
In the quarter-finals, they will face South Korea’s world No 1 pair Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae, who defeated Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King 21-14, 21-16 in 33 minutes in their second-round tie.
World No 4 women’s doubles pair Pearly Tan-M Thinaah booked their last-eight berth after defeating compatriots Carmen Ting-Ong Xin Yee 21-14, 22-20 in a hard-fought match lasting 46 minutes.

Pearly-Thinaah, who won the Denmark Open last week, will face world No 9 Bulgarian sisters Gabriela Stoeva-Stefani Stoeva in their last-eight match today. The Malaysian pair have beaten Gabriela-Stefani in four of their five encounters so far.
Mixed doubles shuttlers Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing have also booked their spot in the quarter-finals, where they will meet Germany’s giant-killers Marvin Seidel-Thuc Phuong Nguyen.
The 27th-ranked German duo beat world No 2 Chinese pair Jiang Zhen Bang-Wei Ya Xin and Malaysia’s ninth-ranked pair Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai Jemie in their first two rounds.
67eab7fd8239add6: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia are assured of at least one men's doubles semi-finalist at the French Open after Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun set up an all-Malaysian quarter-final showdown with Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik on Friday.
World No. 11 Wei Chong-Kai Wun booked their place in the last eight after overcoming Japan's eighth seeds Takuro Hoki-Yugo Kobayashi 25-23, 21-14 in 41 minutes at Arena Grand Paris on Thursday.
The Malaysians held their nerve in a closely fought opening game before taking control of the second to secure their second consecutive victory over the former world champions.
Having lost their first two meetings since 2022, Wei Chong-Kai Wun have now levelled their head-to-head record at 2-2, following their victory over Hoki-Kobayashi at last year's Malaysia Masters.

Their reward is a meeting with compatriote Aaron-Wooi Yik, who advanced without taking to the court after Thailand's Peeratchai Sukphun-Pakkapon Teeraratsakul withdrew from their second-round encounter.
Aaron-Wooi Yik, who finished runners-up at last week's Denmark Open, hold a 5-3 head-to-head advantage over Wei Chong-Kai Wun.
The former world champions also won their most recent encounter at the All England quarter-finals in March, prevailing 21-16, 20-22, 21-14.
Meanwhile, sixth seeds Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin also reached the quarter-finals after finally getting the better of Denmark's Daniel Lundgaard-Mads Vestergaard.
The world No. 5 battled to a 21-6, 14-21, 21-18 victory in 50 minutes, snapping a two-match losing streak against the Danes.
It was their fifth meeting this year alone, with Sze Fei-Izzuddin having suffered defeats in the Malaysia Masters final and China Open second round.
Thursday's victory also levelled their overall head-to-head record at 4-4 and secured a second consecutive French Open quarter-final appearance.
Sze Fei admitted the Danes' strong serving had disrupted their rhythm after a dominant opening game.
"Their service was too good in the second game. That totally disrupted our rhythm," said Sze Fei in a post-match interview with the Badminton World Federation.
He also revealed that both players had been dealing with minor injuries before heading to Denmark last week.
"We had some minor injuries before Denmark, so we just tried to enjoy the game and do our best," he said.
However, a much tougher challenge awaits as they face world No. 1 and top seeds Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae of South Korea.
The Koreans lead their rivalry 4-2 and won their last two meetings, including a 21-16, 21-16 victory in the World Championships quarter-finals in August.
Sze Fei-Izzuddin, however, can draw confidence from having beaten Won Ho-Seung Jae in three games at the Indonesia Open semi-finals in June.
Sze Fei was also pleased to see three Malaysian men's doubles pairs reach the quarter-finals.
"It's a good sign for Malaysian badminton. I think we're on the right track," he said.
The Koreans advanced after ending the campaign of Arctic Open champions Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King, winning 21-14, 21-16 in 33 minutes.
Despite the defeat, the newly formed Malaysian combination can take encouragement from their promising start on the European swing, having secured their breakthrough in Finland earlier this month.

cbdc96c0b569b889: LONDON: UK military helicopters and planes will be equipped to fight wildfires, prime minister Andy Burnham announced late Thursday ahead of hosting England's first "resilience" summit focused on the growing threat they pose.

English firefighting services will also get additional specialist wildfire teams and lightweight personal protective equipment, as the government said it was earmarking up to £45 million (US$60 million) to counter the increase in blazes.
The UK has faced widespread droughts, extreme heat and resulting wildfires each summer in recent years, in a trend scientists have blamed on man-made climate change.

One blaze in Stourbridge, central England, in August gutted 19 houses and damaged 18 others, prompting Burnham to warn on a visit there that Britain must face up to the changing climate and accelerate its clean energy transition.
However, the UK leader has faced criticism from environmental campaigners this week after approving plans to start new drilling within a controversial North Sea gas field.
Also this week a watchdog committee of lawmakers warned recent summers have shown Britain lacks preparedness and the ability to respond effectively to wildfires.

Burnham will on Friday convene fire chiefs, local leaders and experts in Liverpool, northwest England, for the first wildfire resilience summit that his government said would ensure "this summer's scenes are never repeated".
"I stood in Stourbridge and watched families lose everything - I will never forget it," Burnham said in comments released ahead of the event.
"Crews will now have the kit they need to stay safe and military aircraft will stand ready to help tackle wildfires from the sky."
However, Friends of the Earth campaigner Sienna Somers noted the "irony" hosting the summit just days after approving the Jackdaw gas project, which she called "a completely unnecessary carbon-bomb".
"We cannot keep pouring fuel onto the fire," Somers said.

"Andy Burnham must reject new oil and gas developments and reckless airport expansion, further invest in nature-based solutions to capture and store water, and implement a comprehensive adaptation plan."

Announcing the new measures and funding, the ministry of housing and local government said they would include investing in making landscapes more resilient, with financial support for farmers to fireproof their land.
The military component will see Royal Air Force (RAF) Chinook helicopters and a type of transport aircraft equipped to fight wildfires.
They will deploy when requested, to help firefighting crews nationwide battle blazes on "remote moorland, steep hillsides and other hard-to-reach terrain", the ministry noted.

dcfb53d029e382f8: Last week it was Atletico Madrid and Lisandro Martinez; this week Como and Bruno Fernandes.
Another defeat in Europe, another voice in the dressing room feeling compelled to cry out.
Such insubordination would once have meant instant dismissal even for the stellar likes of Roy Keane and David Beckham.
But today, a geological age of anguish later, almost all fans and probably most players feel the complainant is stating the obvious.
For many of the bedraggled army that still follow United in Europe, the sentiment was not for sacking another manager, but for removing the hierarchy.
You would hope that the richest United fans might resort to a revival of the Red Knights that tried to wrest control of the club in 2010.
Mere millionaires came up short last time, but if billionaires were serious, and fans make life difficult for Ratcliffe, you never know.
Beckham is a billionaire now. In 2010, he wore a green and gold scarf to give his support. He needs to rustle up a few rich cronies.
Club captain Fernandes did bring tactics into it, which are at Michael Carrick’s door, but the loathing for the ownership is ratcheting up several notches.
If losing at Atletico Madrid could not be compared to Grimsby or the recent home loss to Brighton after a two-goal lead, Como is in a league of its own.
As recently as 2019, Como were in Italy’s Serie D playing at a communal stadium with a capacity of just over 1,000.
They are managed by Cesc Fabregas, who is remembered as much for throwing pizza at Sir Alex Ferguson as for his spells in midfield with Arsenal and Chelsea.
At the ‘Battle of the Buffet’, it was just a slice; this was the whole pizza, deep-pan with lots of topping.
Como were all over them and United didn’t deserve even a late consolation.
To have progressed to Europe’s premier competition under a rookie manager in that time is a salutary tale for United. Another one.
In between these losses, United managed a creditable draw at Leeds, but they have won only two of ten games this season.
They are a precarious 21st in the Champions League table.
They’re on course for the second-round playoffs, but not a million miles from the ignominy of elimination (positions 25 to 36).
In the EPL, they are 13th, but play Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa, Arsenal and Liverpool next.
No one is predicting a surge up the table.
We pretty well know what will happen next. Carrick will cling on till December, eking out the odd result.
Jim Ratcliffe will say he’s “fully supportive” while interviewing all the usual suspects.
And so it goes on.
As the fans are all too painfully aware, changing the manager doesn’t work.
With the exception of Tommy Docherty’s five-year reign, United has had only two successful managers since the Second World War.
Matt Busby, appointed in 1945 – delayed while he completed military service – and Fergie in 1986.
Looking at the names post-Fergie, they should have done better. David Moyes is still at it with Everton, having led West Ham to a European trophy.
Louis van Gaal is one of the giants of the era and, despite illness, took the Netherlands to a quarter-final loss on penalties to Argentina in the 2022 World Cup.
He was sacked immediately after winning the FA Cup with United and blames City’s “cheating” for his demise.
Jose Mourinho is now at Real Madrid, but he did win the League Cup and Europa League. United were not that bad in those days.
Ralf Rangnick lasted only months as an interim, but it’s widely accepted that he was “sacked” by Ronaldo.
Where was the hierarchy? Where were the Glazers?
And where were they when Rangnick gave his list of players he wanted United to sign?
Avert your gaze now, United fans, as it could be painful reading. Among them were: Erling Haaland, Luis Diaz, Julian Alvarez, Enzo Fernandez, and Josko Gvardiol.
With those and under his astute guidance – he was mentor to the likes of Jurgen Klopp, Thomas Tuchel and Julian Nagelsmann – United could have outdone City.
And there are two more. Between the outbursts by Martinez and Fernandes, Erik ten Hag took a swipe as well.
The Dutchman revealed that he’d wanted Harry Kane and Declan Rice, but his request fell on deaf ears.
Fergie had famously said he’d suffered more pain dealing with Spurs chairman Daniel Levy than from his hip operation, so chief executive Richard Arnold and football director John Murtough didn’t try.
Even though Kane was desperate for the move!
Ditto West Ham and Rice. The Hammers didn’t want to sell, but Arsenal managed to prise their star asset away a year later for £110m.
With those seven players, United would have had a side to take on the world.
Ten Hag also partly blames City for his sacking, but in the period of City’s illegal £900m spending spree, United matched them almost pound for pound, totally above board.
But the Glazers surpassed that figure, taking out an estimated £1.5 billion in dividends and interest.
Absentee owners, incompetent directors. Enter Ratcliffe and the Politburo.
Where the Glazers treat United as a cash cow, to Ratcliffe it’s a hobby horse.
The billionaire sports fan loves to dabble in several and involves his petrochemical company, INEOS.
But unfortunately for him and his many victims, he has the Sadim touch – the opposite of Midas. Or, what has been dubbed the INEOS Curse.
In football, French club Nice have had seven managers in five years while Swiss club Lausanne suffered relegation before coming back up.
The dominant SKY cycling team lost their way when INEOS took over, as did Mercedes in F1 as soon as INEOS sponsorship came in.
Britain’s America's Cup sailing challenge ended in humiliation and litigation after Ratcliffe took over.
Even the mighty All Blacks suddenly became vulnerable with Ratcliffe’s backing.
Cash cow or hobby horse? Between them, the owners have cooked up a real dog’s breakfast.
It’s time for the Red Knights to ride again.
